clue.text: Coming first in a US election

definitions.meaning: first in order or importance, as in a chief or prime concern
an American vote in which a party picks its candidate before the main contest

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: earliest or chief in rank, and the US party nominating contest.

clue.text: Uncommon pronoun

parts.note: a pronoun used by a monarch, who is not a commoner, to mean themself

explanation.definitionFit: The monarch's plural for 'I' is used only by royalty, hence not used by commoners.

clue.text: It's made with a billiard cue — straight up!

definitions.text: It's made with a billiard cue — straight up!

parts.words: It's made with a billiard cue — straight up!
parts.note: a stroke in billiards played with the cue held almost vertical to swerve the ball

explanation.definitionFit: A massé is a billiards shot struck with the cue nearly upright to put heavy spin on the ball.

clue.text: A hot rod driver

parts.note: a worker who hammers heated metal pins into place, joining plates in shipbuilding

explanation.definitionFit: A riveter drives hot rivets, the heated rods that fasten metal plates.

clue.text: Vessel going round lake casts off

indicators.note: the vessel's letters go round the outside of the lake's, holding it

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship, a vessel
a lough is an Irish lake

explanation.surface: A ship sails round a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: LOUGH is the Irish word for a lake, like the Scottish loch.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake sloughs, or casts off, its old skin: a verb synonym.

clue.text: General method that allows margin for error

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
a way is a method of doing something

explanation.surface: An army commander's approach leaves room for mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is room to manoeuvre, a margin or allowance for error.

clue.text: Such investment gives one confidence

parts.note: a unit is one single thing
trust is confidence placed in someone

explanation.surface: This kind of investment makes the investor feel secure.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit trust is a pooled investment fund, so it is an example of investment.

clue.text: It's divine embracing girl in time off

indicators.note: the sacred word embraces the girl's name, holding it inside

parts.note: holy means divine, sacred
Ida is a girl's name

explanation.surface: It is heavenly to hug a girl on a break from work.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday is a period of leave from work, a synonym for time off.

clue.text: The Marathon, perhaps?

parts.note: Marathon was a battle in ancient Greece, and the long race is run in its memory

explanation.definitionFit: A running battle is a long-continued fight; Marathon was a battle commemorated by a race.

clue.text: A word of approval for those in favour

definitions.text: A word of approval for those in favour

parts.words: A word of approval for those in favour
parts.note: in a parliamentary vote the members saying yes are counted under a single word that also means yes

explanation.definitionFit: In a division, the votes in favour are counted as the yes votes, so the word names those supporters.

clue.text: Poorly valued live entertainment

indicators.note: poorly means badly done, so the letters are set out badly in a new order

explanation.surface: Critics rate a live show low.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaudeville is a kind of variety stage show, an example of entertainment.

clue.text: Man on watch around Beach Head

indicators.note: the lookout word goes around the other letter, holding it

parts.note: someone on watch is alert, keeping a lookout

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A man keeps a lookout on a headland by the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beach Head' looks like one military term but splits: the head of Beach is B, placed inside ALERT by 'around'.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert is a man's name; a crossword 'man' is often any male forename.

clue.text: When high water is low

parts.note: a time when the tide's high-water mark is at its lowest of the lunar month

explanation.definitionFit: A neap tide has the smallest range, so its high water is lower than usual.

clue.text: Fruit in tree can go off

indicators.note: to go off is to go bad or explode, so these letters break up and reform

explanation.surface: Fruit on a tree or in a tin can spoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but is part of the fodder: IN, TREE and CAN rearranged by 'go off'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned peach, an example of fruit.

clue.text: Dealing with team capsized in river

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go in the river's name

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands

indicators.note: capsized means overturned, so the letters are tipped over into a new order

explanation.surface: A rowing team overturns its boat in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'capsized' hints at a reversal, but the letters needed are EATM, a jumble rather than a straight turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is the way one deals with someone or something, as in treatment of a subject.

clue.text: Docks associated with locks, we hear

indicators.note: says the word is to be heard, so the spelling changes to match the sound

parts.note: keys are the things used with locks

explanation.surface: Docks on a canal sit beside lock gates.
explanation.walkthrough: On a canal, docks and locks really do go together, which hides the door-lock sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Quays are landing places where ships tie up, a synonym for docks.

clue.text: A shade of caution

parts.note: the colour of the middle traffic light, warning drivers to prepare to stop

explanation.definitionFit: Amber is the yellowish-orange colour of the warning traffic light, a shade signalling caution.

clue.text: Doctor to tell stories about dramatist

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
telling stories means telling fibs, to lie
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A doctor fibs about a playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière was the great seventeenth-century French writer of comic plays, a dramatist.

clue.text: Courts get rough with bad kidnappers

indicators.note: to rough something up is to knock it about, so the letters are roughed into new order

explanation.surface: Bad people are treated roughly by the courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get rough with' suggests punishment; 'rough' shuffles COURTS and BAD, 'get' and 'with' link.
explanation.definitionFit: Abductors carry people off by force, the same as kidnappers.

clue.text: Reveals United Nations' demand in writing

parts.note: UN is the abbreviation for the United Nations

indicators.note: the request goes inside the manuscript abbreviation

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
to ask is to demand or request

explanation.surface: The UN puts its demand on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To unmask is to expose or reveal what is hidden.

clue.text: Desert folk struggle to succeed

parts.note: to rat is to desert, as a rat leaves a sinking ship
a race is a people or folk

explanation.surface: Nomadic people of the desert struggle to thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like the noun of sand dunes but is the verb, to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the competitive struggle to get ahead in working life.

clue.text: Keep your thanks in check

indicators.note: the thanks go inside the restraining word

parts.note: to rein is to check or hold back
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.definitionFit: To retain is to keep hold of something.

clue.text: Badly handle patients' outing?

definitions.meaning: to treat someone cruelly or roughly
read as two words, a treat or day out for the sick

explanation.definitionFit: Ill-treat means abuse, and split it reads as a treat for sick people.

clue.text: Climbs Everest and Ararat, say

definitions.meaning: goes up, as a rider gets onto a horse
examples of mountains, called Mount Everest and Mount Ararat

explanation.definitionFit: To mount is to climb up, and a mount is a mountain, as in Mount Everest.

clue.text: It's very much used as a prefix

definitions.text: It's very much used as a prefix

parts.words: It's very much used as a prefix
parts.note: a Latin word meaning beyond or extremely, placed in front of other words to intensify them

explanation.definitionFit: Ultra- is a common prefix meaning extremely, as in ultra-modern, and is very much used.

clue.text: Joint accompaniment?

parts.note: a joint is a roast cut of meat, and the side dish served with it

explanation.definitionFit: Greens and roast potatoes are served alongside the joint of meat at a Sunday roast.

clue.text: Means of transport, sometimes sprung

definitions.meaning: a light two-wheeled carriage pulled by a pony
a snare whose jaws are set off, or sprung, when touched

explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a pony carriage, and an animal snare that is sprung to catch prey.

clue.text: Small dining chairs

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
dining means eating

explanation.surface: Little chairs for a dining room.
explanation.definitionFit: Seating is the collective term for chairs and places to sit.

clue.text: Cinders gets wicked dame feeling guilty

parts.note: cinders and ash are both what is left after burning

indicators.note: wicked is a slang word for wild, so the letters run wild

explanation.surface: Cinderella's wicked stepmother, a pantomime dame, feels guilty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cinders' is Cinderella in pantomime, with a dame in the cast; here it is ASH, and 'wicked' makes AMED from DAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashamed means feeling shame or guilt for something done.
